newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Elekta says finishes Philips deal.
newsitem.headline: Elekta says finishes Philips deal.

text.p: Swedish medical technology firm Elekta AB said on Thursday it would issue new shares and that a deal with Philips Electronics N.V. to merge the two companies' radiation therapy activities was complete.
"The proposed new issue is expected to bring the company around 310 million crowns," Elekta said in a statement.

It said the purpose of the new share issue was to finance Elekta's "continued growth, ongoing investments within product development, marketing investments, acquisitions as well as to offer improved possibilities for customer financing."
The new share issue was subject to approval at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on February 13.
It also said that a deal with Philips, announced in November 1996, had now been completed.

The deal means that Elekta will pay $60 million, in addition to a possible sales commission to Philips based on order value on condition that a few large specific orders are received before the end of June, 1998.
"This provision is today estimated to cost $25 million," Elekta said.
Financing for the deal will take place through bank loans, the new issue and a new issue placement directed at Philips.
"Philips will apply for newly-issued B-series shares in Elekta worth $20 million based on market price and will thereby become a significant shareholder in Elekta," Elekta said.
For the new issue, to which shareholders have first rights, Elekta said it was proposing an offer of four old shares for one new share.
"If the issue is fully subscribed there will be an additional 237,500 A-series shares and 1,736,795 B-series shares," Elekta said.
